title: HighMorph: De Novo Cyclic Peptide Sequence Design via Protein-Protein Interaction Recapitulation.
authors: Lan, Minhui; Zhang, Chengyun; Wang, Wentong; Hu, Haomeng; Lin, Huitian; Cao, Sen; Guo, Jingjing; Duan, Hongliang
one_liner_zh: 提出HighMorph框架，结合蒙特卡洛树搜索与Transformer网络，利用蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用信息从头设计靶向结合环肽的序列，属于蛋白质结构计算设计领域的方法创新。
abstract: Cyclic peptides have emerged as a compelling class of bioactive scaffolds, but de novo design of target-binding cyclic peptides from protein structures remains challenging. Here, we present HighMorph, an interaction-guided framework that combines protein-protein interaction information with artificial intelligence for rational cyclic peptide design. HighMorph integrates Monte Carlo tree search with a Transformer-based policy-value network to efficiently explore cyclic peptide sequence space, while incorporating explicit atomic-level hydrogen bond constraints extracted from reference protein-protein complexes to guide sequence optimization. The framework is systematically validated on two clinically relevant targets, programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) and kallikrein-related peptidase 4 (KLK4). Notably, 33.3% and 40% of the generated candidates are active against PD-L1 and KLK4, respectively, with active cyclic peptides exhibiting micromolar binding affinities (approximately 10-6 M). These results validate our approach for cyclic peptide design. Additionally, interaction analysis provides insights for developing therapeutics targeting challenging protein interfaces.
abstract_zh: 环状肽已成为一类引人注目的生物活性支架，但从蛋白质结构从头设计靶向结合环状肽仍具挑战性。在此，我们提出HighMorph，一种交互引导框架，将蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用信息与人工智能相结合，用于合理的环状肽设计。HighMorph整合了蒙特卡洛树搜索与基于Transformer的策略-价值网络，以高效探索环状肽序列空间，同时纳入从参考蛋白质-蛋白质复合物中提取的显式原子级氢键约束，以引导序列优化。该框架在两个临床相关靶点——程序性死亡配体1（PD-L1）和激肽释放酶相关肽酶4（KLK4）上进行了系统验证。值得注意的是，33.3%和40%的生成候选物分别对PD-L1和KLK4具有活性，且活性环状肽表现出微摩尔级结合亲和力（约10⁻⁶ M）。这些结果验证了我们用于环状肽设计的方法。此外，相互作用分析为开发靶向挑战性蛋白质界面的治疗药物提供了见解。
